draft.title: Mao Zedong Thought
card: Classical Marxism expected revolution to come from the urban working class, called the proletariat. China in the 1920s was mostly a farming country, with few factory workers.
Mao Zedong adapted communism to these conditions. He saw the peasants, who made up most of China's people, as the main force for revolution.
Mao's views were shaped by his study of rural Hunan, where he saw peasants angry about high rents, debt and landlord power. He believed they could be organised to fight.
This approach is called Mao Zedong Thought. It joined Marxist ideas to Chinese conditions, and it placed peasants, not city workers, at the centre of the revolution.
draft.remember: Mao changed the Marxist plan for China: peasants, not city workers, would drive the revolution.

a.q: Why did Mao Zedong place peasants at the centre of revolution in China?
opts: China was mostly rural, with few factory workers
Peasants had always been the strongest communists
Marxism said revolution must begin in the countryside
City workers were not allowed to join the Party
a.why: China was mostly a farming country with few factory workers, so Mao looked to the largest group, the peasants. The option about Marxism is wrong because classical Marxism looked to city workers, and Mao adapted it.
a.clue: Think about who made up most of China's population.

b.q: A student says that Mao Zedong Thought was simply the original Marxist plan applied without change. Why is the student wrong?
opts: Mao shifted the main role from city workers to peasants
Mao rejected Marxism and made peasants the ruling class
Mao relied on the urban working class more than Marx did
Mao copied the plan directly from the Guomindang
b.why: Mao kept Marxist ideas but adapted them to China by making peasants, not the urban proletariat, the main revolutionary force. The tempting option about rejecting Marxism is wrong because Mao adapted communism and did not abandon it.
b.clue: Who did classical Marxism expect to lead revolution, and who did Mao choose?

a.best: China was mostly rural, with few factory workers

b.best: Mao shifted the main role from city workers to peasants
